> Music week is circuits that turn voltage into sound.A USB MIDI controller on a custom PCB. Touch the copper keys to play notes, press the switches for drums, and turn the knob for volume. It plugs into a computer over USB-C and shows up as a MIDI instrument, so it works with music software like FL Studio, Ableton or LMMS.

## Design

### 2026-10-25: MIDI Keypad: progress so far

**8.22h**

MIDI Keypad: progress so far

I’m building a USB MIDI controller on a custom PCB, based on Kai Pereira’s Hack Club tutorial. It plugs into a computer over USB-C and works as a music instrument.

Planning: I chose a Waveshare ESP32-S3-Zero as the brain, with:
7 capacitive touch keys (copper pads on the PCB that act as piano keys)
3 Kailh Choc low-profile switches for drum sounds
1 EC11 rotary encoder for volume
3 SK6812 MINI-E RGB LEDs
I left out the slide potentiometers to keep the cost down.
Setting up KiCad: I installed KiCad 10 on Ubuntu, added the Hack Club parts library, and cleaned up some old broken library links from a previous project.
Schematic: I wired every part to the MCU using net labels:
Touch keys on GP7–GP13
Switches on GP4–GP6
Encoder on TX/RX

LEDs chained from GP3, powered from 5V
I added power flags so the electrical rules check passed with 0 errors.
Custom footprint: the touch keys don’t exist as a ready-made part, so I made my own footprint: 7 piano-key pads, 10 × 30 mm each, with 1 mm gaps.
